items.citingTitle: The association of statin therapy and cancer: a meta-analysis.
items.reason: Title keyword only; needs human verification
items.reviewedBy: Humanity Loop main worker — independent publisher and full-text source review
items.reviewSummary: Publisher retracted Lee et al. 2014 (DOI 10.1038/bjc.2014.283) on 2026-10-22 over overlapping Figure 3B/3C sections. Chen et al. 2023 (DOI 10.1186/s12944-023-01955-4) cites it as reference [3] only in the Introduction for a preclinical antiangiogenic mechanism. The review's eligibility criteria restrict pooled evidence to prospective randomized human statin trials with cancer outcomes; Table 1 enumerates 35 RCTs, none Lee et al. 2014. Therefore the citation is a verified background reference to a subsequently retracted paper, NOT evidence that retracted study data entered the meta-analysis. No demonstrated effect on pooled cancer-incidence or mortality estimates; do not imply the meta-analysis is invalid or contact editors on this basis alone.
items.nextAction: No external inquiry on this citation alone. Retain as low-priority background-reference update candidate only if journal issues a relevant notice or further evidence shows substantive dependence.

items.reviewSummary: The citing systematic review lists Patano et al. (2023) in its references; that work is itself a scoping review, whereas the citing review reports 10 included primary studies (2 cohorts, 1 case-control, 7 case reports). This supports bibliography citation but does not establish that the cited work was included among the 10 primary studies or that the clinical conclusion relies on it. Publisher's indexed original currently displays a 2025 correction; the queue's purported 2026 notice DOI was not independently retrievable/verified as a retraction during this review. Do not notify authors, infer invalid conclusions, or call this a confirmed retraction until the actual notice and citation context are verified.
items.nextAction: Verify publisher notice DOI 10.3390/jpm16110542 from an authoritative accessible source; if a true retraction, review any narrative reliance on the cited scoping review before considering neutral editorial outreach.

items.citingTitle: The Co-Occurrence of Temporomandibular Disorders in Patients Diagnosed with Tinnitus: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis.
items.reason: Title keyword only; needs human verification
items.reviewedBy: Humanity Loop main worker — independent publisher retraction notice and citing-review text/table verification
items.reviewSummary: MDPI retracted Patano et al. (2023), a mandibular-crowding scoping review (DOI 10.3390/jpm13050774), on 2026-10-23 for major methodological flaws. Bury et al. (2025), DOI 10.3390/jcm14061836, cite Patano as reference [8] in their Introduction to support a tentative statement that mandibular crowding may contribute to tinnitus. The citing review pooled eleven observational studies on TMD/tinnitus co-occurrence; the retracted scoping review is not among those eleven and contributed no identified numerical data to the reported prevalence or odds estimates. This is a verified narrow narrative/background citation dependency, not proof the meta-analysis estimates are affected. Retraction postdates the citing review.
items.nextAction: Do not allege compromised pooled estimates or send an immediate editorial inquiry. On 2026-11-06, check the exact Bury review for any reader-facing citation update and consider a proportionate, human-reviewed clarification only if the specific introductory claim remains materially misleading.
